extracted.intended_audience: literate early-18th-century readers interested in manners, theatre, and moral criticism (readers of The Spectator)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and critical principles for composing and judging satirical/moral essays, theatrical criticism, and social-manners commentary (as modelled in The Spectator essays).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid malicious lampoons and secret stabs to reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: There is nothing that more betrays a base, ungenerous Spirit, than the giving of secret Stabs to a Man's Reputation. Lampoons and Satyrs, that are written with Wit and Spirit, are like poison'd Darts, which not only inflict a Wound, but make it incurable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use wit or ridicule to inflict private injury or to stir up sorrow in a private person; avoid anonymous or malicious attacks that expose families to derision. Talent for ridicule in the hands of ill-natured people becomes especially mischievous; satire ought not to be employed to wound virtue and merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satire should target vice, not virtuous merit
rubrics_metrics.description: If, besides the Accomplishments of being Witty and Ill-natured, a Man is vicious into the bargain, he is one of the most mischievous Creatures ... His Satyr will then chiefly fall upon those who ought to be the most exempt from it. Virtue, Merit, and every thing that is Praise-worthy, will be made the Subject of Ridicule and Buffoonry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When composing satire, avoid making virtuous or meritorious people the butt of ridicule; good satire should focus on genuine vice or folly rather than attacking the innocent or praiseworthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theatre should represent human life and nature
rubrics_metrics.description: There is very little which concerns human Life, or is a Picture of Nature, that is regarded by the greater Part of the Company. The Understanding is dismissed from our Entertainments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plays ought to picture nature and human life; entertainments that ignore human truth and understanding (appealing only to improbable, monstrous, or incoherent situations) produce mere 'laughter of fools' rather than true comic or tragic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scenes of madness must represent disturbance of a noble mind, not mere appetite
rubrics_metrics.description: There are noble Instances of this Kind in Shakespear; but then it is the Disturbance of a noble Mind, from generous and humane Resentments ... I will not mention that we had an Idiot in the Scene, and all the Sense it is represented to have, is that of Lust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When dramatizing madness, present it as a humane, noble disturbance (as in Shakespeare), not as base appetites or comic excess; otherwise the scene becomes ridiculous rather than tragic or moving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actors must understand the passions they portray
rubrics_metrics.description: It certainly requires a Degree of Understanding to play justly; but such is our Condition, that we are to suspend our Reason to perform our Parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective acting depends on the actor's understanding of the passions and motives they portray; playing passions without that understanding reduces performance to caricature or mechanical gestures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performances and recitatives must be intelligible to the audience
rubrics_metrics.description: The Words were no sooner out of my Mouth, when a Serjeant knock'd me down, and ask'd me if I had a Mind to Mutiny, in talking things no Body understood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Language, recitative, and textual clarity are necessary in performance; if lines are unintelligible or styles (e.g., recitativo) are obscure, the audience cannot appreciate the drama and it degenerates into nonsense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advancement in the theatre ought to reflect merit (not absurdity)
rubrics_metrics.description: This is to let you understand, that the Play-House is a Representation of the World in nothing so much as in this Particular, That no one rises in it according to his Merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique of theatrical practice: roles and advancement should be determined by merit and fitness for parts rather than by absurdity, impudence, or mere boldness; practitioners should be mindful of assigning parts suitable to actors' real abilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personification and improbable narrators are effective comic devices
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters are given from Persons like the wild Boar that was killed by Mrs. Tofts, a Chair, a Flower-pot, etc., each complaining or petitioning in human terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using non-human narrators or unlikely perspectives (animals, inanimate stage-furniture) is an explicit comedic device here; such personification satirizes the theatre and provides comic contrast, and can be used deliberately for humour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impudence is a breach of good-breeding; modesty is necessary for beauty and wit
rubrics_metrics.description: No, no Man shall be allowed the Advantages of Impudence, who is conscious that he is such: If he knows he is impudent, he may as well be otherwise; and it shall be expected that he blush, when he sees he makes another do it: For nothing can atone for the want of Modesty, without which Beauty is ungraceful, and Wit detestable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In social conduct and comic character-drawing, impudence should be condemned; deliberate impudence (especially self-conscious) is unattractive and undermines both beauty and wit—writers and commentators should mark it as an anti-pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: To correct impudence, confront the offender in defence of the offended
rubrics_metrics.description: I know no other Way to obviate so great an Evil, except, in the Case of fixing their Eyes upon Women, some Male Friend will take the Part of such as are under the Oppression of Impudence, and encounter the Eyes of the Starers wherever they meet them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical remedy offered: a friend should openly confront a 'starer' (impudent starer) so that the offender experiences shame; public corrective action is proposed when admonition alone will not reform the impudent.

rubrics_metrics.name: True impudence often springs from ignorance; national varietals of impudence exist
rubrics_metrics.description: A true and genuine Impudence is ever the Effect of Ignorance, without the least Sense of it. Impudence in an Englishman is sullen and insolent, in a Scotchman it is untractable and rapacious, in an Irishman absurd and fawning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When depicting comic characters or diagnosing social faults, consider that impudence often arises from ignorance; attributing culturally specific flavours of impudence can be used to sharpen character sketches (but the passage is descriptive rather than prescriptive).

rubrics_metrics.name: To avoid provoking envy, downplay one's perfections and reveal imperfections
rubrics_metrics.description: Having throughly considered the Nature of this Passion, I have made it my Study how to avoid the Envy that may acrue to me ... Upon hearing in a Coffee-house one of my Papers commended, I immediately apprehended the Envy that would spring from that Applause; and therefore gave a Description of my Face the next Day ... being resolved as I grow in Reputation for Wit, to resign my Pretensions to Beauty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical self-presentation tactic: to reduce the malice of envious observers, intentionally disclose humble or unflattering details about oneself (or occasionally be dull) so as to blunt envy and provide consolation to the envious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parents should match children's professions to talents rather than parental inclination
rubrics_metrics.description: Parents take a Liking to a particular Profession, and therefore desire their Sons may be of it. Whereas, in so great an Affair of Life, they should consider the Genius and Abilities of their Children, more than their own Inclinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As social advice (and a practical criterion for career guidance in essays): encourage alignment of vocation with natural abilities; avoid imposing learned professions (divinity, law, physic) on children unsuited to them—trade may better employ many talents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commerce/trade absorbs multitudes better than learned professions
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the great Advantage of a trading Nation, that there are very few in it so dull and heavy, who may not be placed in Stations of Life which may give them an Opportunity of making their Fortunes. A well-regulated Commerce ... flourishes by Multitudes, and gives Employment to all its Professors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Societal/economic criterion: when advising on occupations or composing social commentary, note that trade accommodates many more dispositions and talents than crowded learned professions; this is an argument for recommending commercial pursuits for pragmatic livelihood.
